reasoning:
Cable 1 Kelvin pair is bilaterally unrouted — both /SENSEC1_HI and /SENSEC1_LO carry open ratlines — driving kelvin_unrouted=1 and gate_fail=1. DRC=34 adds further failure mass. The compiler's stub list targets exclusively /CAN_H, /I2C_SCL, and /I2C_SDA, which have zero overlap with the failing Kelvin nets, triggering the Rule-39 compiler_zero_failing_net_overlap condition. All 7 stubs were consumed (absorbed=6, trimmed_spurs=1, total=7=n_stubs), so FR received no guidance for the nets that actually need it. Rules 33, 34, 36, and 39 should be force-injecting Kelvin stubs with mandatory_kelvin_bypass to compensate — this round's data does not confirm they are being bypassed correctly through every consumption stage.

One genuine gap identified: Rule 37 (per-net absorption ceiling) increments net_absorption_count only on absorption events, not on spur-trimming events. In this round one stub was disposed via trimmed_spurs, not absorbed. If /CAN_H, /I2C_SCL, or /I2C_SDA have been repeatedly spur-trimmed across prior rounds instead of absorbed — an equally wasteful outcome that delivers zero routing benefit — their Rule-37 count never reaches the exclusion threshold of 5, keeping them permanently eligible for compiler targeting and permanently draining stub capacity. This is the same leakage Rule 37 was designed to close, accessed through a different disposal path that Rule 37 does not track.

No scorer penalty is warranted: kelvin_unrouted=1000, gate_fail=1000, unconnected=450, and drc=75 are well-calibrated for this failure mode. Raising any penalty would not address the structural issue — the compiler is not targeting the failing nets, so scoring pressure on those metrics does not feed back into stub selection.
manager_rule: Extend Rule 37's net_absorption_count accounting to include spur-trimming events: after each round in which the trimmed_spurs counter is greater than zero, inspect the per-stub records produced by the spur-trimmer to identify the specific net name(s) of every stub classified as a spur and trimmed. For each such net N, increment net_absorption_count[N] by 1, applying the same exclusion threshold (5), the same exclusion conditions (N is not a /SENSEC{M}_HI or /SENSEC{M}_LO Kelvin net, not a USB or CAN differential-pair net, not currently appearing in failing_reasons with unconnected ratlines), and the same exclusion action (add N to compiler_excluded_nets) as Rule 37 specifies for absorption events. Log 'per_net_spur_trim_count_toward_absorption_ceiling' with fields: (a) round number, (b) net name N, (c) net_absorption_count[N] after increment, (d) the round numbers in which N was previously spur-trimmed. Rationale: a stub trimmed as a spur consumes the same compiler stub slot as an absorbed stub and delivers equally zero routing benefit; Rule 37 closes the absorption leakage path but leaves the spur-trim leakage path open, allowing a net that is repeatedly spur-trimmed rather than absorbed to permanently drain compiler capacity without ever triggering exclusion. This rule is additive to Rule 37 and does not replace or defer any action Rule 37 independently mandates.
